title: Ethical Influence and Manipulation Defense
description: Influence is getting someone to want to do what you want. Manipulation is getting them to do it without fully understanding the decision, often using deception or psychological pressure.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Influence is getting someone to want to do what you want. Manipulation is getting them to do it without fully understanding the decision, often using deception or psychological pressure.

sections.title: How Manipulation Appears in Negotiation
content: Good-cop/bad-cop: One person pressures, the other acts friendly, making you lower your guard.
Artificial scarcity: 'We only have two slots left at this price.' The scarcity may be fake.
Reciprocity trap: A small, unsolicited concession early ('I'll include delivery at no charge') creates pressure to concede later on a bigger issue.
Personal flattery: 'You're the best negotiator I've faced' primes you to be generous.

sections.title: Protection Strategies
content: Recognize the pattern and label it silently: 'This is a classic good-cop/bad-cop setup.'
Call a break to disrupt the momentum. Say: 'I need a few minutes to think.'
Return to objective criteria: 'Can we base this on the data we both agreed to use?'
Use a broken-record technique: calmly repeat your core requirement without getting drawn into emotional back-and-forth.

sections.title: Common Mistake
sections.content: Trying to 'out-manipulate' the manipulator. It escalates, damages your reputation, and rarely ends well.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: The best defense against manipulation is not being a better manipulator. It's being someone who recognizes the game and refuses to play by its rules.
